question: The issue of accounting for scope 3 emissions for leased goods raises questions about who is responsible for these emissions and how to account for them fairly. Under the current sustainability reporting standards, the company purchasing a new product, such as a car, has to report all the upstream scope 3 emissions, even if the company is only leasing the product for a limited share of that product’s lifetime.
I would therefore like to ask the Commission to elaborate on how the implementation of the CSRD will deal with this: 1.
When a company leases a new car or van, is it obliged to report the total upstream scope 3 emissions in the financial year of the purchase?

When determining who should bear responsibility for reporting the emissions, how does the Commission distinguish between cases where the lessee has operational control (operating lease) and those where the lessee has financial control (financial leasing)?

Is the Commission considering an approach whereby a company that leases a vehicle for a limited share of that vehicle’s lifetime can divide the upstream scope 3 emissions across the vehicle’s lifetime and thus only report the emissions corresponding to the lease period?
answer: European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS) require companies to disclose emissions from each significant Scope 3 category, according to the principles of Greenhouse Gas Protocol (GHGP). ESRS only requires a company that leases a new vehicle to report the total upstream scope 3 emissions in the financial year of purchase if they are deemed material.

The company must make this judgment in its materiality assessment process. EFRAG, the Commission’s multistakeholder advisory body on ESRS, has published guidance on materiality assessment and established a questions and answers platform to answer technical questions (1).

When the lessee has operational control and the asset is not recognised in its balance sheet (operating lease), it should report the Scope 1 and 2 emissions associated with the operation of the asset within Scope 3 Category C ‘Upstream leased assets’. In this case the lessor should report the emissions under its own Scope 1 and 2 emissions.

When the lessee has operational control and the asset is recognised in its balance sheet (financial lease), it reports the Scope 1 and 2 emissions associated with the operation of the asset within its own Scope 1 and 2, as per ESRS rules. In this case the lessor should report the Scope 1 and 2 emissions of the leased assets within its Scope 3 Category C ‘Downstream leased assets’.

The Commission is not considering an approach whereby a company that leases a vehicle for a limited share of that vehicle’s lifetime can divide the upstream scope 3 emissions across the vehicle’s lifetime and thus only report the emissions corresponding to the lease period, since for upstream leased assets these are not emissions required to be reported for Scope 3 Category C ‘Upstream leased assets’ as per the GHGP rules.
